body:
READ-ONLY PINNING PREFLIGHT, NO MODEL DOWNLOAD PERFORMED.

The IBM candidate is identifiable but the stock runtime is not yet reproducible enough for our receipt.

- transition-amr-parser master currently resolves to 6edc0f116ebc906a49b780eae665a9ed860b4f73. Its package metadata is 0.5.4 with Apache-2.0 code and pins Torch 1.13.1, NumPy <= 1.23.5, and fairseq 0.10.2 on Linux.
- PyPI 0.5.4 publishes source SHA-256 3cc721d326f5bb1d6ddcdc3fe050037ec54913c1b2f7b765df0c8333ecd836b2 and wheel SHA-256 45023e32d554ece5d1aa8ed47b6d3924c652b90af67cfbcece566104549242bf.
- The parser-model-hub main pin is 97e592a55e5d8c1c2faaea0ff2ef47d512c8f145. AMR3-structbart-L maps to amr3.0-structured-bart-large-neur-al-seed42.zip, 1,268,268,872 bytes, LFS SHA-256 f503fd95b98710feeebd6c225078e9b15c0743076383717eb8fee0c74bb33e67. The model repository has a root Apache-2.0 license, but I found no per-checkpoint model card; that distinction belongs in the intake record.
- Load is not closed by those pins. At the exact parser SHA, SentenceEncodingBART hard-codes torch.hub.load of pytorch/fairseq bart.large. That is a second mutable network fetch not named by the AMR checkpoint. The checked-in Dockerfile also expects preloaded DATA and is a recipe, not a published image digest.

RULING I PROPOSE: stock AMRParser.from_pretrained is inadmissible for the scientific spike. The runtime must either use a recorded overlay that loads separately pinned local BART bytes inside a base image pinned by digest, with the overlay itself hashed, or stop as RuntimeDependencyUnpinned and compare amrlib. I will not spend the roughly 1.27 GB checkpoint download plus BART cache before chief disposition of the architecture and this pinning risk.
